Railway’s Security Incident: Why CI/CD Needs Runtime Security

Railway’s incident shows that a compromised CI/CD build can expose broader internal credentials and cloud access, making build isolation, egress controls, and tightly scoped OIDC trust essential. The article promotes StepSecurity Harden-Runner for runtime visibility and outbound network enforcement in GitHub Actions environments.
KEY POINTS
  • 01Railway reported that an attacker partially escaped build isolation, obtained a build credential, accessed build histories and internal source, and later used a separate OIDC configuration error to gain cloud access.
  • 02Railway stated that at most 1.85% of workspaces, approximately 100,000, could have had customer variables decrypted, and described this as an upper-bound estimate.
  • 03The article recommends isolating untrusted build jobs from privileged deployment jobs, using disposable execution environments, and limiting access to internal services and production credentials.
  • 04StepSecurity Harden-Runner provides runtime network and process monitoring with workflow-step context and can enforce reviewed outbound destination allowlists on supported runners.
  • 05The article recommends placing production cloud credential jobs behind GitHub environments with required reviewers and binding cloud trust policies to the intended repository and protected environment.

Railway’s November 10, 2026 incident report describes an October 20–21 attack in which an attacker partially escaped build isolation and obtained a build infrastructure credential. Railway said misplaced trust in that credential enabled access to stored build histories and its internal source. A separate OIDC configuration error later enabled cloud access and access to credentials and systems used to retrieve and decrypt customer variables. Railway estimated that up to 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000, could potentially have had variables decrypted, while emphasizing that this was an upper-bound figure.

The article argues that CI/CD build jobs are a security boundary because they execute code, handle credentials, and can access networks, services, artifacts, and deployments. It recommends separating untrusted builds from privileged deployment jobs, using isolated disposable runner environments, restricting access to internal services, and reviewing credentials inherited from runner hosts. It also recommends observing and restricting outbound connections, validating OIDC trust and cloud permissions, and placing production credential jobs behind protected GitHub environments with required approval. The article presents StepSecurity Harden-Runner as a tool for runtime network, process, and supported file-write visibility, as well as outbound network policy enforcement.

  • A workflow can appear narrowly permissioned while still being risky if its runner host exposes inherited credentials, cached material, or access to internal services.
  • Network restrictions should be tested against real workflow behavior, including dependency downloads, artifact uploads, deployment endpoints, and failure-handling paths, before they are enforced.
  • A cloud role tied to a protected deployment environment should deny access to jobs that omit that environment, even if those jobs run in the same repository.
  • Moving file-change checks and other unrelated third-party Actions into a separate low-privilege job can keep them out of the job that receives production cloud credentials.
  • Outbound allowlists limit where a runner can connect, but they do not prevent an allowed service from being misused or govern stolen credentials used from another machine.

The article examines Railway’s report that an attacker broke out of part of its software-building environment, obtained internal access credentials, and later reached systems used to retrieve and decrypt customer variables. Railway said up to 1.85% of its workspaces, about 100,000, could potentially have had stored variables decrypted, although this was an upper estimate. It matters because software-building systems often hold access keys and can connect to important company systems, so a compromise there can affect customers and production services. The article recommends separating build jobs, limiting where they can connect, and requiring explicit approval before software-building jobs can access production systems.

A malicious Windows authentication component designed to steal passwords, password hashes, and login tokens.

A malware component that targets the Windows LSASS process to steal login credentials from memory.

A SOCKS5 proxy malware component that relays attacker traffic through compromised systems.
Corelight organization
Corelight is a cybersecurity company that provides network detection and response products.
corporate accounts concept
Corporate accounts are user accounts that belong to a business or are used for work purposes.
Coruna malware
Coruna is a named malware family, cyber tool, or threat label referenced in security reporting.
counterterrorism concept
Counterterrorism means efforts to prevent, disrupt, or respond to terrorist activity.
crafted Microsoft Office file technique
A Microsoft Office document intentionally made to trigger a vulnerability when someone opens it.

Crafted request technique
A specially formed message sent to a server or application in an attempt to trigger a particular response or flaw.
credential concept
A credential is proof of identity for logging in, such as a password, security token, API key, or certificate.
credential collection technique
The process of harvesting usernames, passwords, and tokens, typically by malware or phishing, to gain unauthorized access.
Credential Disclosure concept

Credential Reuse technique
Using stolen or previously exposed usernames and passwords to try to access other accounts or systems.
credential rotation technique
Credential rotation means replacing passwords, keys, or tokens with new ones to reduce the risk from stolen or old credentials.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-harvesting

also: credential harvester, credential-harvesting protection
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
Credit Card Data concept
Information from payment cards that can be used to process transactions or commit fraud if stolen.
Credit Card Details concept
Payment-card information such as a card number, expiration date, and security code.
Credit Card Information concept
Credit card information includes card numbers and related details that can be used to make payments.
Credit card numbers concept
Credit card numbers are payment card identifiers that criminals try to steal for fraud.
Creduz malware
Creduz is a named malware family referenced in security reporting.
criminal groups threat-actor
Groups of people organized to commit crimes.
critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.
critical issues concept
Critical issues are problems considered urgent because they can cause major harm, such as system compromise or serious service disruption.
critical remote code execution vulnerability
Critical remote code execution is a severe security flaw that lets an attacker run code on a system from afar.
critical systems concept
Critical systems are important systems whose failure could seriously affect operations or safety.
critical vulnerabilities vulnerability
Critical vulnerabilities are very serious security flaws that could let attackers cause major damage or gain major access.
cron tool
cron is a Unix tool that runs scheduled commands or scripts automatically at set times.
cross-site scripting vulnerability
Cross-site scripting is a website vulnerability that lets attackers run malicious scripts in other users’ browsers.
cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability

cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
also: crypto

The use of a computer's processing power to generate cryptocurrency, often without the owner's permission.
also: botnet and cryptocurrency miner activity
Cryptocurrency seed phrases concept
Cryptocurrency seed phrases are secret recovery words that can give full access to a crypto wallet.
cryptocurrency wallet product
A cryptocurrency wallet is software or hardware used to store and use the keys that control digital coins.
Cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases concept
These are secret recovery words that can restore and fully control a cryptocurrency wallet.
cryptocurrency wallets product
Cryptocurrency wallets are tools used to store and manage access to digital currency funds.
cryptojacking technique
Cryptojacking is when attackers secretly use someone else’s computer power to mine cryptocurrency.
Cryptomining technique
Using computer processing power to generate cryptocurrency, often without the system owner's permission.
CSS protocol
CSS is the web language used to control how pages look, including colors, fonts, and layout.
Cumulative updates concept
Cumulative updates are software updates that include current fixes plus earlier fixes in one package.
also: cumulative update
Customer Account concept
A personal account that lets a customer sign in to a company's service and manage their information.
Customer accounts concept
Customer accounts are user records and logins that let customers access a company's services.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer database concept
A customer database is a stored collection of information about an organization's customers.
Customer environments concept
Customer environments are the computers, cloud services, networks, and settings used by an organization.
customer information concept
Customer information is data a business keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, purchases, or account records.
Customer Records concept
Stored information about customers, such as names, account details, and contact information.

A CVE identifier is the standard public tracking number assigned to a known cybersecurity vulnerability.

CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS 10.0 concept

CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS Scores concept
Standard numerical ratings used to describe the technical severity of software vulnerabilities.
CVSS v3.1 Score concept
A standardized numerical rating used to show how severe a software vulnerability is likely to be.
CVSSv3 concept
CVSSv3 is version 3 of a scoring system used to rate how severe a software vulnerability is.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber capabilities concept
Cyber capabilities are the tools, skills, access, and processes an organization or country can use in cyberspace.

An online identity associated with a threat actor in security reporting.
cyber operations concept
Activities conducted in cyberspace including espionage, sabotage, or defense, typically by state-sponsored groups.
cyber response window concept
The amount of time an organization has to detect, contain, and respond to a cyber incident.
Cyber risks concept
Cyber risks are the chances that digital systems, data, or services could be harmed by accidents, failures, or attacks.
cyber verification program concept
A cyber verification program is a process for checking that security claims, controls, or requirements are actually in place.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
CyberAveng3rs threat-actor
A threat-actor identity linked in public reporting to Iranian cyber activity targeting industrial systems.
cybercrime concept
Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers, networks, or the internet.
cybercriminals threat-actor

cyberespionage technique
The use of computer networks to conduct espionage, usually by state-sponsored groups to steal secrets from governments or corporations.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) organization
A U.S. government agency that helps protect civilian government systems and critical infrastructure from cyber threats.
cybersecurity researchers organization
Cybersecurity researchers are people who study digital threats, software flaws, and attacks to help protect systems.
CyCognito organization
CyCognito is a cybersecurity company known for external attack surface management technology.
CyScenarioBench tool
A cybersecurity benchmark used to measure how well an AI system handles security-related tasks and restrictions.
Daily Cyber Headlines product
A recurring news resource that summarizes cybersecurity headlines.
Danfoss organization

dark mode concept
Dark mode is a display setting that uses darker colors to reduce brightness.

also: DarkSword exploit chain
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
data breach concept

data container concept
A storage area used by an app to hold its files, settings, and other data.
also: app's data container
data leak sites concept
Data leak sites are websites used by criminals to publish or threaten to publish stolen data.

Data Protection API, often called DPAPI, is a Windows feature that helps applications encrypt and protect secrets for a user or machine.
Data Quality concept
A measure of whether data is accurate, complete, current, and useful.
Data Sources concept
Data sources are systems, services, or devices from which information is collected.
Data Storage concept
The keeping of digital files and information on devices or online services.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
database query concept
A request sent to a database to retrieve, add, change, or remove information.
datasets concept
Datasets are collections of information that researchers or tools analyze to find patterns and evidence.

Dates of birth are personal information that can help identify someone and may be sensitive if exposed.

Dawn means the early morning period around sunrise and may be used to describe when an event happened.

defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.

Scheduled periods when refrigeration equipment melts accumulated frost or ice.

Controls that determine when and how refrigeration equipment removes frost buildup.

Defused Cyber organization
Defused Cyber is a cybersecurity organization or service name associated with cyber threat intelligence and security research.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
demo concept
A demo environment is a system set up to demonstrate software or features, rather than serve real users.
democratic processes concept
The activities and institutions through which people choose representatives and make public decisions, such as elections.

dependencies concept

dependency concept

detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detections concept

The computers, services, and tools used to create, test, and improve software.

Disaster recovery is the process of restoring technology systems and data after a major failure, attack, or disaster.

distinct() technique
A data-processing operation that removes duplicate entries from a dataset.

A company that makes electronic controllers and monitoring products for refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment.

droppers malware

A threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.

egress concept

email collection technique

encoding concept
Encoding is changing data into a particular format so computers can store, send, or interpret it.

encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.

Requests sent to a website or web service using encryption, usually HTTPS, so others cannot easily read them in transit.

End to end means something is handled across the whole process from start to finish, often without gaps between steps.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
engagement concept
Engagement means how often people interact with a website, app, message, or notification.

Enterprise services are business IT systems or applications used across an organization.

enumerate technique

environment variables concept

eset

europe

european-union
The European Union is a political and economic union of European countries that also creates cybersecurity and privacy rules.

Automated tasks that test, assess, or process data in a computing environment.

exfiltrate technique

exploit technique

exploitation technique

fable-5 product

wallet concept

wallets product
Wallets are apps, devices, or accounts used to store and manage cryptocurrency keys and funds.

watchOS product
Apple's operating system for Apple Watch devices.

An Apple Watch operating-system update.

Watering-hole attacks compromise websites that targets are likely to visit so attackers can infect or track them.
weaknesses concept
Security problems or gaps that could be used to compromise a system.
weaponized concept
Weaponized means something harmless-looking has been modified so it can be used to attack or compromise a target.

Wi-Fi passwords concept

Wi-Fi profiles are saved network settings that help a device reconnect to known wireless networks.
windows product

Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 product
Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 is a long-term servicing edition of Windows 10 for organizations.

Windows 11 26H2 product

A Windows server service that stores organization user accounts, computers, and access permissions.

A Windows networking feature that lets multiple devices share an internet connection by translating network addresses.

windows-10 product

windows-11

Wiz organization
A cloud security company that helps organizations identify and remediate risks in their cloud environments.

workaround concept
A workaround is a temporary way to avoid or reduce a problem without fully fixing its root cause.
workflow concept
A workflow is a series of steps or tasks that are followed to get something done.

Workflows are automated sequences of steps that move data, trigger actions, or run tasks across systems.
workforce concept

A security research organization referenced in security reporting.
zero-click technique

zero-day
